title: Incredible Machine
study: Actual researchers, computer graphics, synthesized speech and computer-made music.
application: Ground the opening in people experimenting with instruments. Pair a hand operating equipment with the image that equipment makes.
status: Source notes and sampled film frames reviewed

title: North by Northwest — titles
study: Graphic lines align with the window grid of a real building.
application: Use the reverse relationship: the horn photograph and its drawing share actual edges. Preserve that correspondence across the transition.
status: Sequence breakdown reviewed; full film not viewed

title: Walking City
study: An architectural figure retains a continuing identity while its material and form evolve.
application: Establish a movement and silhouette that belong to the horn, then let its construction change around that identity.
status: Artist description and installation still reviewed

title: Powers of Ten
study: A journey in scale whose successive views remain related to a known starting point.
application: Keep the viewer oriented during camera movement. Every change in scale needs a remembered physical reference.
status: Official description reviewed; watch link collected

title: Universe
study: Scientific imagery reaches beyond what an ordinary observer can see; NFB identifies it as a source for 2001.
application: Study the feeling of an instrument extending human perception and the contrast between physical apparatus and vast subject matter.
status: NFB description and poster reviewed

title: Catalog
study: Early computer-related abstraction made with repurposed analog military equipment.
application: Look for disciplined repetition and variation: several lines following one intelligible rule. Avoid independent decorative paths.
status: Museum account reviewed; full film not viewed

title: Pixillation
study: The archival record describes crystal-growth footage interspersed with computer patterns.
application: Connect physical experimentation and mathematical imagery through material and rhythm. A reference for mixing media without a pile of floating cards.
status: Smithsonian record reviewed; no film download

title: IBM Think
study: Material studies in paper craft, architecture, light, dimension and perspective, rooted in one recognizable wordmark.
application: Give the horn several material states while preserving its identity. Study folded surfaces and the readability of the original form.
status: Studio breakdown and two stills reviewed

title: Apollo S-band deployment
study: A packaged mesh antenna opens through a sequence of mast, leg, rib and reflector operations.
application: Use actual hinge and rib relationships to choreograph the unfolding. The new opening should be produced by connected parts.
status: Deployment text reviewed; linked old images/clip are broken; NASA training photo retrieved separately

title: Echo inflation test — P-03600
study: Inflation Tests of the Echo 1 Satellite in Weeksville, N.C.
application: Large folded material becoming an instrument. Study seams, tension and the human scale at its base.
status: NASA metadata and downloaded photograph reviewed

title: Echo inflation test — P-03603
study: Inflation Tests of the Echo 1 Satellite in Weeksville, N.C.
application: The material surrounds its makers. Study folds, reflections and the contrast between people and an enormous experimental surface.
status: NASA metadata and downloaded photograph reviewed

title: Echo inflation test — P-03598
study: Inflation Tests of the Echo 1 Satellite in Weeksville, N.C.
application: A long vertical strip inside a hangar makes scale readable. Useful for a material pulling through the frame.
status: NASA metadata and downloaded photograph reviewed

title: SMAP deployable reflector
study: A modern deployable mesh reflector; mechanically relevant, outside the archival period.
application: Reference for opening a rim and tensioning a membrane. Keep its modern date explicit.
status: JPL description reviewed

title: Helpers — original reference
study: Wireframe, edges, normals, tangents, bounding boxes and an orbiting camera.
application: Retain the intricate scientific drawing and depth. Use only the helpers that carry meaning.
status: User-provided source code and screenshot reviewed

title: NURBS surfaces
study: A curved surface described through weighted control points.
application: A small set of shared controls can shape neighboring horn panels together.
status: Source page reviewed

title: Morph targets
study: Blend geometry between authored target shapes.
application: Create a small number of deliberate horn poses. Preserve vertex correspondence and design the path between poses.
status: Example page and BufferGeometry documentation reviewed

title: Skinning / articulated structure
study: A skeleton controls mesh vertices through weights.
application: Use a rig for ribs and folding panels when mechanical articulation matters; rigid parts can use parented pivots.
status: Source page reviewed

title: Line2 / controlled line width
study: Thick lines with controllable width.
application: Differentiate silhouette, structural seams, and the quiet interior grid.
status: Source page reviewed

title: Orthographic camera
study: Object size remains constant with distance.
application: Useful for a precisely aligned drawing pose. An orthographic trace is an artistic reconstruction, not automatic recovery of the photographed 3D object.
status: Source page reviewed

title: AnimationMixer.setTime
study: Seek an animation to a specific time.
application: Make the motion reproducible so every exported frame can be checked and revised.
status: Source page reviewed

title: Ordinary Folk — process
study: Message, design, animation and audio considered as a production process.
application: Select visual evidence and test the handoff in rough motion before adding finish.
status: Source page reviewed

title: Sander van Dijk — transitions
study: Treat the scenes as moments of a continuous performance; find a common rhythm and test rough animatics.
application: Choose the persistent motion for the horn sequence before designing isolated shots.
status: Source page reviewed

title: Match cuts
study: Continue framing, shape or action across an edit.
application: The photographed rim and its drawn rim should share position, scale and motion at the handoff.
status: Source page reviewed

title: Ordinary Folk / Webflow breakdown
study: A production account with design frames, a composition graph and an effect removed because it did not fit the message.
application: Use a short motion study to decide whether the horn transformation communicates curiosity or only attractive deformation.
status: Source page reviewed

title: Ordinary Folk — project files
study: Shared rigs and project files for waves, path warping and delayed movement.
application: Study controllable relationships and overlapping timing. Native project files have not been opened here.
status: Source page reviewed
